This implies that 2,4,6-Trimethylhepta-1,3,6-triene may act through a pathway involving Seneciphylline, which modulates M-phase phosphoprotein 8. The mechanism appears to involve a chain of targets, where the compound may influence the activity of SDR family member 9, which then affects M-phase phosphoprotein 8. The evidence supports a potential regulatory role for 2,4,6-Trimethylhepta-1,3,6-triene in the functional activity of M-phase phosphoprotein 8, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
